ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS  
Revival of sick PSEs by BRPSE  
*561. SHRI C. RAMACHANPRAIAH: Will the Minister of HEAVY 
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sect or Enterprises 
(PSEs) is responsible for the revival of sick PSEs; 
(b) if so, how many PSEs have been revived during the last three years; 
(c) whether any time-bound programme is in place to revive the ailing units; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES 
(SHRI SONTOSH MOHAN DEV): (a) to (e) A Statement is  laid on the 
Table of the House. 
*Not recorded. 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
.   Statement  
(a) Government had constituted Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector 
Enterprises (BRPSE) in December, 2004 as a part-tim e advisory body to 
advise the Government on the strategies, measures a nd schemes related 
to the strengthening, modernization, reviving and r estructuring of Central 
Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs). 
(b) Based on the recommendations of BRPSE, Government h ave 
approved the proposals for revival of 25 cases of C PSEs through revival 
package/Joint venture/disinvestment/merger and clos ure of one CPSE 
involving total assistance of Rs. 7660 crores in the form of fresh infusion of funds, 
waivers/write offs, etc. In addition, Government ha ve also approved revival 
package for Nagaland Pulp & Paper Co. Ltd. envisagi ng total assistance of Rs. 
788 crores from Government in the form of fresh infusion of funds, waivers/write 
offs, etc. 
(c) to (e) The administrative ministries/departments pr epare a 
comprehensive package for revival/rehabilitation or closure of loss making CPSEs 
after due consultations with all stakeholders. The administrative 
ministries/departments process the recommendations of BRPSE for obtaining 
the approval of the Government. The decisions of the Government on the revival or 
otherwise of the sick CPSEs are implemented by the concerned administrative 
ministries/departments. The concerned ministries/de partments have been 
advised to expedite submission of the proposals in respect of the sick CPSEs under 
their control for consideration of BRPSE. BRPSE has  also been advised to 
expedite their recommenda{ions in respect of the pr oposals pending with 
them. The concerned administrative ministries/departments have further been 
advised to process the recommendations of BRPSE expeditiously for obtaining 
the approval of the Government.

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
SHRI SONTOSH MOHAN DEV: Sir, the BIFR was supposed to be 
closed. But, unfortunately, there has been a Supreme Court intervention in this 
decision, and, hence, the work of the BIFR has not been stopped it is continuing. 
The replacement of the BIFR by another Act is not there. The BIFR is doing its 
duty and, without its permission, on those cases which are under the BIFR, the 
BRPSE cannot take a decision. The Board of Reconstr uction takes decision 
only in those cases which are not in the BIFR. But their recommendation goes 
to the BIFR. In many of the cases, the BIFR agrees, and thereby those companies, 
which are recommended by BRPSE and accepted by the BIFR, are being 
revitalised. It is being done even in his State in Andhra.

revived.

New airports and training centres in NER 
*562. SHRI URKHAO GWRA BRAHMA: Will the Minister of  CIVIL 
AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Planning Commission has approved six new 
airports in the North Eastern Region including the BTAD area of Assam; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether his Ministry will contemplate policy to set up new institutes or 
training centres in some unused old airports including Rupsi of Assam on the 
lines of Pilot Training Centre, Ground Engineering Institute or Air Hostess 
Training Centre etc.; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
(SHRI PRAFUL PATEL): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid  on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement  
(a) and (b) The Planning Commission has approved the construction of only 
one Green-field airport in the North Eastern Region i.e. at Pekyong in Sikkim. The 
proposals for new Greenfield airports near Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) and at 
Cheitu (Nagaland) are under examination. 
(c) and (d) The development projects in North Eastern States are taken up at the 
request of and in consultation with North Eastern Council (NEC). There is no 
proposal from NEC for the establishment of Pilot Tr aining Institute etc. at 
Rupsi. 
The guidelines for setting up Pilot Training Instit utes and Aircraft 
Maintenance Engineering Training Institutes have already been laid down by the 
Government. 
(e) Does not arise. 
SHRI URKHAO GWRA BRAHMA: Sir, connectivity has been  a major 
problem in the North-Eastern region. Many times, the Civil Aviation Ministry has 
assured the people of North-East that connectivity will be improved and 
priority will be given to set up new airports. In h is reply, the hon. Minister has 
clarified that only one Green-field project has bee n approved by the Planning 
Commission in the North-Eastern region. But, in the district from which I come, 
the Bodoland Territorial District area in Assam, there is a hue and cry that a new 
airport will be set up and for that purpose, land a cquisition is also going on. 
Thousands of people are going to be evicted. There is a major problem now. We 
know that six airports have been approved by the NEC.I have come to know that the 
Planning Commission has also agreed, in principle, to set up six new airports in 
the North-Eastern region. But, I do not know the reason... 
MR. CHAIRMAN: What is your question? Please, put your question. 
SHRI URKHAO GWRA BRAHMA: I would like to know from the hon. 
Minister whether these six new airports are really going to be set up or not. 
And, if such proposal comes to the Ministry, what w ill be the response of the 
Ministry? 
12 

[15 May, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
SHRI PRAFUL PATEL: Mr. Chairman, Sir, hon Member ha s some 
factual data which is not in accordance with what I  have got. The Planning 
Commission has only approved one Green-field airport, and two airports —one at 
ltanagar in Arunachal Pradesh and the other at Cheitu in Nagaland — are under 
examination. The one that has been approved is a Pekyong in Sikkim. So, I do not 
know that six new airports, which he has mentioned, are at which stage. But, I 
can assure the hon. Member that as far as airports are concerned, there are 22 
operational airports already in the North-East, and  if we include Bagdogra, it 
comes to 23, and if these three airports, one-plus-two are approved, it will take 
the number to almost 26 airports. I think it is a v ast territory in terms of what 
airport you are mentioning. I do not think the Nort h-Eastern Council or the 
Planning Commission has yet given any approval for any airport, or any proposal 
for new airport is under consideration, as hon. Member has mentioned. As far as 
the Ministry is concerned, I can assure you that we are completely in agreement 
that the connectivity of the North-Eastern region s hould be maintained at the 
highest level. That is why, for all these airports,  even though there has been a 
recurring annual loss, the Airports Authority has never shied away from either 
meeting this expenditure or spending large capital expenditure for upgrading and 
developing all these airports in the North-Eastern region. 
SHRI URKHAO GWRA BRAHMA: Sir, second part of my que stion was 
regarding the revival of Rupsi Airport. On 16th Oct ober, 2006, the hon. 
Minister had made it clear that revival of Rupsi Airport was not possible. Now, 
our concern is that there is international border, Indo-Bangladesh border, and 
this airport is lying unused and land is being used  for wrong purposes. It has 
become vulnerable to new encroachment in the area. That is why, I was 
suggesting for setting up new institution. I would like to ask whether in future, 
the Ministry of Civil Aviation would contemplate any such policy to use Rupsi 
Airport under the Airports Authority of India to make it operational. 
SHRI PRAFUL PATEL: As of now, Rupsi Airport is aban doned it is 
virtually misused. It is not in a position, as it s tands today, to be revived. 
However, as I said, we will all take it up with the  North-East Council and the 
Planning Commission and see how we can find a solution. 
SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH SHARMAH: Sir, one-and-a-half year back, we 
had a long meeting of the MPs from North-East with the Civil Aviation

remember, hon. Minister also agreed, at the time, t hat he would consider the 
revival of Rupsi Airport. Sir, Rupsi Airport is one of the oldest airports. It was

SHRI PRAFUL PATEL Sir, I just mentioned in reply to the question put by

SHRI MATILAL SARKAR; Sir, I think, the hon. Ministe r is aware that 
there are proposals from the State Government of Tripura to renovate some of the 
Airports of the State, particularly, Kamalpur, Kailashahar and Khowai. Will the hon.

SHRI PRAFUL PATEL: Sir, various State Governments a cross the 
country, including Tripura, want more and more airp orts to be upgraded and 
operationalised. I would only like to reiterate that as far as the State is concerned, 
Agartala is very busy and an important airport. We are putting in more and more 
investments to upgrade the technology so that it becomes all-weather and more and 
more reliable airport. But in terms of the smaller airports, I think, what is required 
is the concerted efforts by the State Governments a nd I would not only talk 
about Tripura but all the State Governments across the country. Every hon. 
Member wishes that air connectivity.. ( Interruptions)...  
SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: I asked about Kamalpur.. .(Interruptions)...  
SHRI PRAFUL PATEL: Yes, it is in the middle of the city; you would 
appreciate that there are some operational difficul ties also. But, 
simultaneously, for the information of all the Members, I would urge them

MS. PROMILA BOHIDAR: Sir, I would like to know from the hon. Minister

question as this is basically for Airports in the North-East. However, with regard

investments we put in. So, the State Governments are also being requested to look

on the North East are satisfactory and yet, perhaps  not so. Sir, everything is 
related to the State Governments, the Government is  doing something. The 
State Governments have their own limitations in the whole country. They have 
much more limitations in the North East. The proble ms of the North East — 
law and order, tourism, earning, employment and job s — are related in a 
major way to aviation. And, whatever the States of that region may do or not 
do, will the Minister kindly assure the House that he will bend his 
considerable energies which he applies elsewhere in  the country to do 
something positive in his tenure for the North East? 
SHRI PRAFUL PATEL: Dr. Gill is on the Committee of Civii Aviation 
also and therefore, I can assure him that all the 2 2 airports in the North East 
are ultimately in ail these States. There are only three States which do not 
have an airport operational and these are Arunachal  Pradesh, Sikkim and

Nagaland are under examination which will also see the light of the day very 
soon. So, there is no question of putting the respo nsibility on the State 
Government. The Central Government, the Planning Co mmission the North 
East Council and the Airports Authority are doing t heir very best to ensure 
connectivity to every State. And, I can assure you that there is no endeavour 
to pass on the buck to the State Government I am on ly talking of the smaller 
airports about whch additional requirements are bei ng mentioned from time 
to time across the country. I was only referring to that.

Resource crunch in banks  
563. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the unabated credit expan sion has resulted in a 
resource crunch forcing banks to mobilize deposits by raising interest rates; 
(b) whether Government are aware that some of the banks are reported to be 
seeking bulk deposits from other banks at very high interest rates to tide over the 
liquidity problems; and 
(c) if so, the steps being taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (S HRI 
PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL): (a) to (c) A statement is laid  on the Table of 
the House. 
Statement  
(a) Increased returns on competing investment products,  increase in Repo 
Rate, etc. and enhanced demand for credit, have led banks to mobilize deposits at 
higher rates of interest. 
(b) and (c) It is a normal practice for banks to borrow funds from other banks 
in the inter-bank call money market to tide over te mporary mismatches in 
their fund flows. However, to enable Public Sector Banks (PSBs) to advance 
credit to the productive sectors of the economy at reasonable rates of interest, 
the banks have been advised to increase their deposit base, with special focus on 
low-cost deposits. The performance of PSBs in this regard is also being 
monitored, on an ongoing basis, by the Government. 
SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Sir, I have seen the reply of the hon. Minister. In 
addition to that, my first supplementary is, accord ing to the press reports, the 
Government has asked the public sector banks to moderate growth of credit to 
high-risk sectors. The growth of economy continues to exert pressure on 
banks to maintain the rate of credit expansion. The  industrial sector has 
experienced a growth rate of over 8 per cent in recent months. The automobile 
industry, pharmaceuticals and the garment sector ar e enjoying robust growth. 
So, any restriction on credit expansion will result 
17 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007]  
into slowing down of industrial growth. Therefore, I would like to know from the 
hon. Minister whether the Government has directed the public sector banks to 
restrict credit to these sectors. 
SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL: Sir, there is no question of denying 
credit to any sector. The banks have only been advised to see as to which are the 
sectors and how to really modulate their credit por tfolio. The Government is 
conscious of the fact that the manufacturing sector  has played a major role in 
the growth. And, therefore, there is no denying cre dit to the manufacturing 
sector at all. 
SHRIMATI S.G INDIRA: Sir, my second supplementary is this. According to 
reports, the recovery of housing loans advanced by the public sector banks is at 99 
percent and defaulters at less than one percent. However, according to reports, the 
Government has asked the public sector banks to restrict their housing loans. It is the 
dream of an individual to have his home with the help of bank loan. Therefore, I 
would like to know from the hon. Minister whether the Government is considering to 
revise its decision on housing loans, so that the middle-class section can own house 
of its own choice. 
SHRI PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL: Sir, again, I would submit that there is 
no such instruction whatever that the loans to the housing sector should be 
restricted. In fact, it has been emphasised that wh ile they restructure their 
portfolios, the housing sector as such must not suffer. Rather, during the latest 
decision, the priority sector lending loan for the housing sector has been 
increased from Rs. 15,00,000 to Rs. 20,00,000.

Revealing of Participatory Notes holders names by Flls  
*564. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI † 
SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Foreign Institutional Inv estors are not bound to 
reveal the names of Participatory Notes holders whi ch goes against the well 
established concept of 'know your customers', norms practiced world over, 
(b) if so, what are the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that Flls are not allowed  to issue PNs to Indian 
Nationals, persons of Indian origin; 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(e) what steps Government have taken to ensure that terrorists operating from tax 
haven and routing their investments and wrecking ha voc on the Indian stock 
market are not allowed? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (e) A 
Statement is placed on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (d) The Securities and Exchange Board of Ind ia (SEBI) Act, 1992 
empowers SEBI to register and regulate Foreign Inst itutional Investors 
(Flls). Under the Act, SEBI has framed the SEBI (Fl l) Regulations, 1995. 
In terms of these Regulations, an Fll may issue Par ticipatory Notes (PNs) 
with Indian instruments (equity/debt/derivative) as  the underlying securities, 
subject to the subscriber being a regulated entity.  Further downstream 
issueance of PNs, if any, can also be done to regul ated entities only. The 
Regulations also require the Flls, which issue PNs,  to file a report in a 
prescribed format at the end of each month. In this  report, amongst other 
information, the Fll has to disclose the names of a ll subscribers to the 
PNs issued by it. The reporting format also contain s an undertaking wherein 
the Fll declares that it or its associates have not  issued/subscribed/ 
purchased any PNs to/from Indian residents/NRIs/PIO s/OCBs during the 
reporting period. 
†The question was actually asked on the floor of th e House by Shri Abu 
Asim Azmi. 
21 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
(e) Adequate systems and safeguards to deal with il legal activities on the 
Indian Stock market are in place. 
The Foreign Exchange Management Act, (FEMA) 1999 has provisions to deal 
with cases of unauthorized transfer of foreign exch ange including through 
hawala.- 
The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and Rules thereunder have 
come into effect from 1st July, 2006. Under the Act and Rules, banking companies, 
financial institutions and intermediaries are oblig ed to verify the records of 
identity of clients. 
The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, as amended in September, 2004, 
has provisions to combat financing of terrorism. 
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976 (FCRA), also regulates and 
monitors receipt and use of foreign funds by the recipients. 
At the international level, India, is a member of A sia Pacific Group (APG) 
on Anti-Money Laundering and Combating of Financing of Terrorism and has 
Observer status in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

ESOPs for employees  
*571. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:      
SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Employee Stock Option Sch emes are long-term 
benefit given to employees; 
(b) if so, how did Government initiate their coverage under Fringe Benefit Tax 
in this budget without being clear on how they would be valued and taxed; and 
(c) why they should not be more appropriately taxed in the beneficiaries hands? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) Employee 
Stock Option Schemes are undoubtedly benefits given  to employees. 
However, it is not necessary that the benefits are long-term in nature. 
(b) there is no ambiguity in the policy relating to levy of fringe benefit tax on 
Employee Stock Options Plan (ESOPs). 
(c) It is immaterial whether ESOPs are taxed in the hands of the employees 
or the employers as the applicable rate of tax would generally be same for both, 
since ESOPs are generally granted to employees in the higher tax bracket. Further 
in case ESOPs are taxed as perquisite, the employer  will be required to deduct 
TDS from the salary of the employee. On the other hand, in the case of ESOPs 
being taxed as fringe benefit, the employer has to pay the tax but it still has an 
option to recover it from the employee, without att racting any further tax 
consequences.

*572. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the Minister of PETROLE UM AND

(a) whether Government have received any representation from Tamil Nadu 
regarding supply of defective LPG cylinders which m ay lead to risky

(b) if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard;

THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI 
DEORA): (a) and (b) Government have not received an y representation from 
Tamil Nadu Government regarding supply of defective LPG cylinders by Public 
Sector Oil Marketing Companies. 
(c) to (e) At present, three Public Sector Oil Mark eting Companies 
(OMCs), namely Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOC) , Bharat Petroleum 
Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited 
(HPCL) are marketing LPG in the country. 
OMCs are procuring LPG cylinders from cylinder manu facturers who are 
approved by the Oil Industry Technical Committee (O ITC) and have valid 
manufacturing licences from the Bureau of Indian St andards (BIS) and the 
Chief Controller of Explosives (CCOE). Strict control is exercised by BIS over 
the manufacturing process. LPG cylinders procured by OMCs meet the required 
quality standards. 
LPG cylinders are manufactured under the close supe rvision of third party 
inspection agency, viz., BIS, which enforces strict control over the manufacturing process. 
OITC also carries out surprise audit of cylinder manufacturing units to ascertain the 
quality standards of the cylinders. Cylinders received from distributors/transporters 
at the bottling plants are mandatorily checked for quality and genuineness to avoid 
the entry of fake and outdated cylinders in circula tion. On detection, sub-
standard/spurious cylinders are confiscated and the reafter deshaped/crushed to 
prevent their re-circulation.

Amendment of income tax act  
*575. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken note of anomaly in th e matter of 
investments that qualify for reduction from income under section 80 C of the 
Income Tax Act insofar as the investments made in M utual Funds have a lock 
in period of three years whereas fixed deposits with the banks have a lock in 
period of five years; 
(b) if so, whether Government propose to remove the ano maly by 
amending the Income Tax Act during the current Session; and 
43 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (c) 
Section 80C of the Income Tax Act provides a deduction of upto Rs. 1 lakh from 
the gross total income to an individual of HUF, which makes investments in specified 
savings instruments or makes certain specific payments. The savings instruments 
includes Equity Linked Saving Schemes (ELSS) floated by mutual funds and terms 
deposit of a scheduled bank for a period of not less than 5 years. While the lock in 
period in the case of ELSS is 3 years, it is 5 year s in the case of term deposit 
with a scheduled bank. 
Investment in ELSS is essentially an investment in equity while term deposits 
with a scheduled bank are debt instruments yielding assured returns. Therefore ELSS 
carries a significantly higher risk in comparison to a term deposit with a scheduled 
bank. In order to compensate ELSS for the higher risk, a relatively lower lock-in-
period of three years has been provided. 
In view of the above, there is no proposal to amend  Section 80C of the 
Income-tax Act.

which was placed on the website of the Ministry on August 4, 2004 for 
information and comments by stakeholders. Thereafte r, on December 2, 
2004, an Expert Commitee headed by Dr. J.J. Irani w as constituted to subject 
various views/options received to merit evaluation and make recommendations 
to the Government on revision to the Companies Act,  1956. The Committee

Smuggling of antiques and statues  
†4317. SHRI LALIT KISHORE CHATURVEDI: Will the Mini ster of 
CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that smuggling of antiques and statues is taking place 
continuously; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that antiques and statues  are being exported to 
foreign countries through smuggling; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that ASI is not committed  towards the 
presentation and storage of antiques of the country  and it is indifferent also 
towards the same; and 
(d) the action being taken by Government to check t his loot and 
smuggling of antiques of the country? 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI): (a) and (b) 
The availble data does not indicate continuous smuggling and illegal export of 
antiquities to foreign countries. 
(c) and (d) The Archaeological Survey of India is fully committed towards the 
conservation and safety of the antiquities at the protected monuments as well as 
the site museums. To ensure their safety, the Archa eological Survey of India 
engages security guards whose strength has been aug mented by deploying 
private security guards, State police and home guar ds personnel and also the 
CISF at selected monuments. 
Provisions exist under the antiquities and Art Trea sures Act, 1972 for 
regulation of export in antiquities and art treasur es and for prevention of their 
illicit trafficking such as registration of dealers, registration of specified categories 
of antiquities, prosecution of offenders etc. The Government is also amending the 
provisions of the Act to provide additional safety guards against illegal trafficking 
in antiquities.

(b) whether it is a fact that rate of inflation measure s the rate of increase in 
prices and not the actual increase in prices of various items and commodities; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that wholesale price index, consumer price index, 
price index for urban non-manual employees and pric e index for agricultural 
labours do not give real picture of the situation of inflation and actual price rise;

PAWAN KUMAR BANSAL): (a) Sir, the average rate of growth of GDP and 
inflation (WPI based) from 1991 to 2006 is given in  the Statement (See

(b) The rate of inflation measures the rate of increase  in prices and is 
calculated on the basis of an index consisting of various commodities and having 
a weight assigned to each commodity. Based on the r ate of increase in price 
of each commodity and the weight assigned to that c ommodity in the basket, a 
composite rate of inflation is calculated. There ar e, at present, five such 
composite rates of inflation, viz. (i) Wholesale Pr ice Index (WPI), (ii) 
Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW ), (iii) Consumer Price 
Index for Urban Non-Manual Employees (CPI-UNME), (i v) Consumer Price 
Index for Agricultural Labour (CPI-AL) and (v) Consumer Price Index for Rural 
Labour (CPI-RL). 
(c) In case of WPI, the basket is only of selected commodities and the weight 
assigned to each commodity is on the basis of the value of traded amount of that 
commodity. The other indices, which are all variant s of the Consumer Price 
Index, are based on the consumption pattern of the different groups, thereby 
implying different weights assigned to a particular commodity or services in the 
respective baskets. 
(d) In view of the divergent factors affecting the dema nd and supply of a 
particular commodity in different regions of the co untry, it is not possible to 
have a unique measure of the rise in price of a particular commodity for the entire 
country.

use is estimated at 18.1 per cent of total sale of PDS kerosene, no estimation

To check adulteration in auto fuels and diversion o f PDS kerosene, 
Government has asked Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to take various steps 
to contain the menace of adulteration:— 
(i) Under the Control Orders issued by the Governme nt to prevent fuel 
adulteration, under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, State 
Governments are empowered to take action against those indulging in 
adulteration. Government have requested the State 
Governments/Union Territory Administrations to take  steps to 
control adulteration. 
(ii) OMCs undertake regular and surprise inspection s of Retail Outlets 
and also take action under Marketing Discipline Gui delines 
(MDG) and Dealership Agreements against those indul ging in 
adulteration and malpractices. MDG provide for term ination of 
dealership in cases of adulteration being established. 
(iii) Government has taken the initiatives to exped ite the installation of 
Global Positioning System (GPS) to monitor the movement of tank 
trucks. 
(iv) OMCs have introduced new tamper proof tank-tru ck locking 
system to prevent en-route adulteration by transporters. 
(v) Keeping in view the misuse/diversion of SKO for  adulteration, the

number of new initiatives which are given in the Statement. 
162 

[15 May, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
Statement  
Details Of New Initiaves Taken To Check Adulteration Of Petrol/ Diesel 
And Streamlining Pds Kerosene Distribution  
Checking adulteration is a continuous process and t he Ministry of 
Petroleum & Natural Gas has been reviewing steps ta ken to curb adulteration 
from time to time. In the process, several technolo gical and institutional 
measures have been taken to contain adulteration. T he recent steps taken by 
the Ministry are summerized below. 
1. Automation of Retail Outlets: In order to monitor t he activities at retail 
outlets by adopting the latest technological improvements, automation of retail 
outlets is being implemented. MOP&NG has directed t he oil marketing 
companies to complete automation of retail outlets selling more than 200 KL per 
month. 
2. Third Party Certification of Retail Outlets: OMCs h ave been directed to 
complete third party certification of all the retail outlets selling more than 100 
KL per month. 
3. Monitoring of movement of Tank Trucks through Globa l Positioning 
System (GPS): In order to prevent adulteration duri ng transportation, OMCs 
have been directed to install GPS for complete moni toring of the movement 
of all the company owned/dealer owned/ contractor owned tank trucks. 
4. Marker System in Kerosene: To check adulteration in  auto fuels, 
Government has asked public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to take 
various steps, including introduction of marker in adulterants. OMCs have 
commenced introduction of marker in kerosene on all  India basis with effect 
from 1.10.2006. Under the new system, Market is being put in kerosene in all 
depots. This system heralds the introduction of wor ld class technology to curb 
and eventually eliminate the menance of adulteratio n of transportation fuels 
along the supply chain. With the marker's presence, aduteration even with very 
low levels of kerosene can be detected. MS/HSD Cont rol Order, 2005 SKO 
Control Order, 1993 and MDG 2005 have been amended for making provision 
regarding introduction of marker system in Kerosene to check adulteration. A 
committee has been set up in the Ministry to monitor the progress of the marker 
system. Oil Marketing Companies in the Private Sector have also been 
163 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
simultaneously asked to introduce marker in Kerosene as is being done by 
Public Sector OMCs. 
5. Revising the Marketing Discipline Guidelines: The M arketing 
Discipline Guidelines (MDG) under which the oil mar keting companies take 
penal actions against the erring dealers have been revised during August 2005 
making the penal actions more stringent. As per MDG, 2005, a dealership would be 
terminated in the first instance of adulteration itself. 
6. Jan Kerosene Pariyojna: To streamline the PDS Kerosene distribution system 
and contain diversion of kerosene for adulteration and other unauthorized 
usages, Jan Kerosene Pariyojna (JKP) had been launched initially for a period of 
6 months on a pilot basis in 414 blocks with effect  from 2.10.2005. The Pilot 
scheme has been further extended upto 30.6.2007. 
7. Smart Card Scheme: With the objective of ensuring that the benefit of the 
subsidy reaches the targeted consumers in an efficient and cost-effective manner 
and to prevent any leakages, this Ministry has prop osed introduction of Smart 
Card System for distribution of PDS kerosene. The s cheme is proposed to be 
introduced initially on an experimental basis. In t he Pilot project, subsidized 
kerosene through Smart Card is proposed to be evailable to BPL families while all 
other ration card holders would be given non-subsidized kerosene. Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) would ensure adequate availability of PDS as well as non-
subsidized kerosene during the entire period of implementation of the Pilot.

NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA J. PATEL): (a) to (d) Gove rnment of India 
allocates kerosene to the States/Union Territories (UTs) for distribution under 
the Public Distribution System (PDS) on historical basis for the purpose of 
cooking and illumination only. In accordance with t he policy adopted by the 
Government of India in 2000, kerosene (SKO) allocation for distribution under 
the Public Distribution System (PDS) was reduced every year beginning 2001-

Pradesh for increasing the SKO allocation, the Gove rnment of India 
commissioned the detailed study of kerosene demand in the country, through the 
National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) in December 2004.

recommended to restrict the subsidy on kerosene to BPL families only.

Rangarajan, Chairman, Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister to 
examine different aspects of pricing and taxation of petroleum products with a 
view to stabilizing/rationalizing their prices. The Committee submitted its report

subsidy on kerosene to BPL families only. The Gover nment has accepted the 
recommendations of Dr. Rangarajan Committee Report and has decided 'in 
principle' that subsidy on PDS kerosene be limited to BPL families only. The

Constitution of Heritage Sites Commission  
4409.    SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
SHRI B.J. PANDA:                                      
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:  
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government proposes to constitute a Heritage Sites Commission 
as the present legal and institutional framework is  inadequate to address the 
conservation of built heritage in its broadest outline; 
(b) whether the function of the proposed Heritage Sites Commission would 
include advising Government on heritage matters and  framing guidelines for 
conservation of heritage monuments and sites; and 
(c) if so, by when Government is likely to announce its formation? 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI): (a) and (b) 
Yes, Sir. As the present legal and institutional fr amework is not adequate to 
address the documentation, inventorisation and conservation of built heritage in 
its broadest outline, government has proposed to co nstitute a Heritage Sites 
Commission. The Commission would lay down broad policy guidelines and take 
steps to ensure that such guidelines are observed. 
The functions of the proposed Heritage Sites Commission would include: 
— tender advice to Government on heritage matters. 
— frame guidelines in the matter of conservation of heritage 
monuments and sites. 
— study or cause to study important matters regarding conservation of 
heritage and submit reports to the Government. 
— suggest appropriate amendments to the existing heritage 
legislations. 
(c) No time frame can be indicated at this stage.

Water crisis  
†4421. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH: Will the Minister fo r WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are formulating any plan to solv e the problem of 
water crisis; and 
(b) if so, the details thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The 
average annual water availability in the country is assessed a 1869 billion cubic 
metre (BCM). Based on the population of 1027 millio n as per the 2001 
census, the per capita available works out to be 18 20 cubic metre per year. 
However, there is considerable temporal and spatial  variations in the water 
availability in the country and due to population g rowth, the per capita water 
availability is also declining year after year. The re are also instances of over-
exploitation of ground water leading to lowering of water table in certain areas. 
Water being a state subject, several measures for d evelopment and 
management of water resources are undertaken by the  respective State 
Governments which include creation of storages, res toration of water bodies, 
rain water harvesting, artificial recharge to ground water and adoption of better 
management practices etc. Government of India provi des assistance to the 
State Governments for completion of on-going irriga tion projects under the 
Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP). Further, a pilot scheme titled 
"National Project for Repair, Renovation and Restor ation of Water Bodies 
directly linked to Agriculture" has been approved b y Government of India in 
January 2005. Government of India also provides sup port under centrally 
sponsored scheme for Command Area Development and W ater Management 
(CAD&WM) with a view to bridging the gap between ir rigation potential 
created and potential utilized. Government has also constituted an Advisory Council 
on Artificial Recharge to Ground Water under the Ch airmanship of Union 
Minister of Water Resources with the main objective to popularize the concept 
of artificial recharge to ground water among all stakeholders.

originally would have cost Rs. 1,10,242 crore due to delays ranging from one to six

completion of projects results in cost over-run. The other reasons for cost over run are 
inadequate provision in the original estimates, change in the scope of the project mostly 
extension of command area, geological surprises, unexpected increase in the cost of land 
acquisition, Resettlement and Rehabilitation, forest land acquisition,cost escalation of 
construction material, labour etc. In view of normal gestation period of major projects as 10 
to 15 years and that of medium projects as 5 to 8 years, the major projects started during 
or before 1992 and medium projects started during or before Eighth plan which will be 
continuing as ongoing in Eleventh plan may be" considered as delayed projects. As per the

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. 
The Sub-Committee under the Chairmanship of Dr. M.S. Swaminathan submitted 
its report on more crop and income per drop of wate r. Recommendations 
made by this Sub-Committee have been summarized and given in the Statement 
(See below). 
(c) and (d) Artificial Recharge of Ground Water Adv isory Council while

Accordingly, the report of the Sub-Committee will be before the Council in its 
next meeting, However, preliminary action on recomm endations has already

Statement  
Recommendations made by the sub-committee headed by 
Dr. M.S. Swaminathan 'more crop and  
income per drop of water'  
The report of the Sub-committee on 'more crop and income per drop of water' 
highlights that the irrigation water security is vital both for livelihood and food 
security. The report draws attention to the scope a vailable for improving the 
efficiency of use of irrigation water in a manner that both the productivity and 
profitability of farming are enhanced which is the pathway to an ever-green 
revolution all over the country, without associated ecological harm. Important 
recommendations of the Sub-Committee are as follows:— 
* The Sub-Committee recommended observation of Year 2007-08 as the 
'Year of More Crop and Income per Drop of Water to give the strategies 
and their importance in improving the productivity and income per 
unit of water. 
* Adequate provisions in XI Plan for inclusion of the  measures for 
augmentation of water supply should be made. The investment from 
Government as well as from lending Agencies such as World Bank should 
give priority for modernization of the tertiary can als with control 
structures. 
215 

RAJYA SABHA [15 May, 2007] 
* Micro Irrigation technology e.g. drip and sprinkler  irrigation 
including drip fertigation to increase productivity of crops with less 
water should also be popularized. System of Rice In tensification 
technology (SRI) which requires less quantity of se eds, less nursery 
area, saves water and labour and enhance yield is also required to be 
popularized. 
* Introduction of weather based crop insurance for minimizing the losses 
to farmers for safeguarding farmers during weather uncertainties. 
* Implementation of Farmer Participatory Action Resea rch 
Programmes with the help of Agricultural Universiti es, Research 
Institutes, ICRISAT, WALMIs, etc. for triggering a mass 
movement. This Programme can cover 5000 villages in different agro-
climatic regions during 2007-08. The Gram Sabhas in the villages will 
serve as Pani-panchayats and will provide overall g uidance and 
support to this programme. In addition, launching o f water literacy 
movement' and imparting training to one woman and man from every 
panchayat as Water Masters is also suggested. 
* The Water User Agencies (WUAs) should be involved i n the 
decision making so that the maintenance of the stru ctures will be 
made easy. 
* In order to implement successfully the above recommendations, a 3-tier 
setup at Village, State and National level has been  suggested. At 
National level, a Pan Government of India Steering Committee 
consisting of representatives of various Departments which will report 
to-Agricultural Cordination Committee, chaired by t he Prime 
Minister.

Regulation and control of ground water 
4426. SHRI DHARAM PAL SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Central Ground Water Auth ority (CGWA) have 
been constituted to regulate and control ground wat er management and 
development; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) how far Central Ground Water Authority has achieved  the target to 
regulate and control ground water; 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) what concrete steps Government propose to take to solve the shortage of 
ground water and river in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and(b) Yes 
Sir. Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) has been constituted under sub-
section 3 of Section 3 of the Environment (Protecti on)Act,1986 vide & 
notification dated 14.01.1997 and subsequent amendments for the purpose of 
regulation and control of ground water development and management in the 
country. 
(c) The Central Ground Water Authority has undertak en the following 
regulatory measures to control the development of ground water. 
(i) Central Ground Water Authority is regulating withdrawal of ground . 
water by industries/projects in 1065 over-exploited , critical and semi-
critical areas. List of these areas has been circul ated to the State 
Pollution Control Boards and Ministry of Environment & Forests which 
refer the new industries/projects falling in these areas to CGWA for 
obtaining permission. Pre-conditions in case of permissions are mandatory 
adoption of rain water harvesting system, monitoring of ground water 
abstraction as well as monitoring of ground water l evel and quality etc. 
by the industry. 
(ii) CGWA has notified 43 Over-exploited areas in t he country for 
regulation of ground water development and manageme nt. For 
enforcement of the regulatory directions Issued under Section 5 
220 

[15 May, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
of EPA. 1986, concerned Deputy Commissioners/ Distr ict 
Magistrates have been authorized to take necessary action in case of 
violation of directives of CGWA in the notified areas. In these notified 
areas, installation of new ground water abstraction structures is not 
permitted without prior specific approval of the Authority. For more 
effective regulation of ground water development and management, 
Advisory Committee under the Chairmanship of Distri ct 
Collector/Deputy Commissioners have been constituted. 
(iii) Directions have been issued Group Housing Societies, Institutes, Hotels, 
Industries, Farm Houses, etc. in the notified areas  of Delhi, 
Faridabad, Gurgaon and Gaziabad and other areas of NCT Delhi where 
ground water table is below 8 metres from ground su rface to adopt 
roof top rain water harvesting system. The last date for adoption of 
rain water harvesting has been extended upto 30.06.2007. 
(iv) CGWA have also notified 65 over-exploited areas in various States for 
registration of ground water abstraction structures , which showed a 
very steep decline in ground water levels and requi red action for 
regulation. 
(d)Does not arise. 
(e) Several measures for development and management  of irrigation are 
undertaken by the respective State Governments whic h include creation of 
storages, restoration of water bodies, rain water h arvesting, artificial recharge 
to ground water and adoption of better management p ractices etc. 
However,Government of India is providing Central As sistance to the State 
Governments through various schemes/programmes, suc h as Accelerated 
Irrigation Benefits Programmes (AIBP); Command Area  Development and 
Water Management (CADWM) Programme; National Projec t for Repair, 
Renovation and Restoration of Water Bodies directly linked to Agriculture etc. 
The Government of India also encourages rain water harvesting and recharge to 
ground water for conservation of water. The Central  Ground Water Board 
(CGWB), under the Ministry of Water Resources, has also circulated 
Manual/Guide on Artificial Recharge to Ground Water  to the States/Union 
Territories to enable them to formulate area specific artificial recharge schemes 
to check the declining trend of 
221

ground water levels. Ministry of Water Resources have circulated a revised Model 
Bill to regulate and control the development and management of ground water 
to the States/Union territories in 2005.

Interlinking of rivers 
4430. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of WA TER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the world experts have pointed that water flow on glacier-fed rivers will 
decrease substantially in the coming decades due to the effect of global warming; 
(b) whether India propose to have any contingency plan in place by inter-linking 
of its rivers; and 
(c) what follow-up action has been taken on our river inter-linking policy and now many 
agreements have been signed for such projects so far? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) A number of reports 
about the effect of climate change and global warming on water flow have been published 
from time to time. Some of these reports indicate reduction of flows in glacier-fed rivers. 
The report titled "India's Water Economy bracing for a turbulent future" by World Bank 
states that "Climate change is likely to substantially increase overall monsoonal rainfall in India, 
but this is liekly to be poorly distributed in the sense that much of the additional rainfall 
will probably be in high-intensity storm events". 
(b) and (c) The Government of India have formulated a National Perspective Plan 
for Water Resources Development (NPP) in August 1980. The NPP comprises of two 
components viz. (i) Peninsular Rivers Development and (ii) Himalayan Rivers 
Development and envisages construction of storages on various river system along with 
interlinking canal systems to transfer water from water surplus area to water deficit 
regions. National Water Development Agency (NWDA) under Ministry of Water 
Resoruces has been set up in 1982 to study the feasiblity of inter basin water transfer 
proposals and give a concrete shape to NPP. NWDA after various studies identified 30 links 
under NPP (16 Peninsular and 14 Himalayan) for preparation of feasiblity reports. So 
far, NWDA has completed the feasibilities reports for 14 links under Peninsular Component-
and 2 links under Himalayan Component. A tripartite agreement (MoU) between the 
Government of India and concerned States of Madhya Pradesh & Uttar Pradesh was signed on 
25.03.2005 for preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Ken-Betwa link under 
Peninsular Component.
